notes.title: Body idioms
notes.text: Korean uses body words in many expressions: 눈이 높다 ("high eyes" = picky), 발이 넓다 ("wide feet" = knows lots of people), 손이 크다 ("big hands" = generous, cooks huge portions — like Grandma).

notes.title: Saying you're sick
notes.text: 감기에 걸렸어요 (I caught a cold). 열이 나요 (I have a fever). 머리가 아파요 (I have a headache). 배가 아파요 (I have a stomachache). 목이 아파요 (I have a sore throat).

notes.title: Korean pharmacies
notes.text: Pharmacies (약국) are everywhere, marked with a big 약 sign. Pharmacists can recommend medicine for common colds. Clinics (병원, 의원) are quick and inexpensive, and you can usually walk in without an appointment.

notes.title: Porridge for the sick
notes.text: In Korea, rice porridge (죽) is what you eat when you're sick — often abalone or pumpkin porridge. There are whole restaurant chains that sell only 죽.

notes.title: -죠
notes.text: -죠 (short for -지요) asks for agreement, like "…, right?" or "…, isn't it?": 맛있죠? ("It's good, right?"). It also softens statements: 제가 하죠 ("I'll do it, then").
